steps.title: Money that is ready at once
steps.body: Life sends bills without warning. A washing machine breaks. A job ends. An [[emergency-fund]] pays for this. It does not need to grow. It needs to be there at once. Money you can use at once, without selling anything, has high [[liquidity]]. People count the fund in months of costs, often 3 to 6.

stat.label: months of costs, a common size for a safety net

steps.prompt: The boiler breaks. The repair costs €1,500 and is due this week. Where does the money come from?

choices.label: From the emergency fund
choices.ending: The repair costs €1,500, and not a cent more. Over the next months, you fill the fund up again.

choices.label: Use the overdraft
choices.ending: The overdraft charges about 11% a year. Paid back over 12 months, the same repair costs about €1,580.

choices.label: Sell investments in a bad month
choices.ending: The fund is down 20% this month, so you sell at a low price. When prices recover, the shares you sold would be worth about €1,875 again.

steps.prompt: A household spends €2,800 a month. How big is an emergency fund for 3 months?
steps.reveal: €8,400: three months of costs. That is enough to bridge a gap between jobs without borrowing.

steps.prompt: When is this money needed? Swipe each item to the left or to the right.

items.text: Three months of costs if a job ends

steps.explanation: Money needed within a year belongs in the [[emergency-fund]]: safe and ready at once.

steps.prompt: True or false: an emergency fund should grow as fast as possible.
steps.explanation: False. Its job is to be there at once and keep its value. Fast growth comes with swings, and a surprise does not wait for a good day.

steps.title: How long your savings last
steps.body: You spend about **{monthlySpending}** a month. Your savings account holds **{savingsBalance}**. If your income stopped today, that would cover about **{bufferMonths}** months of costs.

stat.label: months of costs your savings cover

steps.title: Your decision
steps.body: Your savings cover about **{bufferMonths}** months of your costs today. How many months do you want as your safety net? You choose the number.
steps.bodyNoData: How many months of your costs do you want to keep as your safety net? You choose the number.

scenes.title: Bills without warning
scenes.desc: An [[emergency-fund]] pays for surprises. It must be ready at once: it needs high [[liquidity]], not fast growth.
